question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: s must be, as a whole, one SIG of the SIG grammar below; anything else -> throws. The tokens are IDENT and the literals ( ) [ ] , : | -> and ... (each literal exactly as spelled: "- >" and ". .." are not tokens). WHITESPACE is optional before, between and after any tokens — so "list [text]", "... xs", "f (a :text)->text" and a SIG broken over lines are all accepted — and it is required only where two IDENTs meet, because an IDENT is read longest first ("pubfn" is one IDENT). No other character is ignored: there is no comment form, so a "#" anywhere throws.

PREFIX is the IDENT token sequence pub fn, or export default function, any WHITESPACE between its words. It is read as a prefix only when another IDENT (the function name) follows it; it occurs at most once. Otherwise no prefix is read and the first IDENT is the function name: "pub(fn: text) -> text" is a function named pub, "export(default: text) -> text" one named export, "pub fn fn(a: text) -> text" one named fn; "pub fn(a: text) -> text", "pub fn" and "pub fn pub fn f() -> none" throw
The name entry is the function IDENT. Each PARAM becomes an argument map in order; a leading "..." marks it a rest parameter and adds rest = true.

TYPE gives a union tree (alts in order) when it has two or more ALTs, else the single ALT's tree. The members of a union are never unions themselves, and a nested TYPE inside brackets is its own tree. A SCALAR ALT gives k = that name; the tuple form gives items, list item, map key and val, record fields as [IDENT, tree] pairs, all in order.

Unreachable alternatives -> throws: within one TYPE (at any nesting level), an ALT that an EARLIER ALT of the same TYPE covers (TABLE COVERS). A later ALT never covers an earlier one, so "text | json" is legal while "json | text" throws; and spacing never matters. COVERS is structural: "list[json] | list[text]", "tuple[json, text] | tuple[text, text]", "map[json, json] | map[text, text]", "list[text | none] | list[text]" and "record[a: text] | record[a: text, b: none]" throw, while "list[text] | list[text | none]", "tuple[json, json] | tuple[text]", "record[a: text, b: none] | record[a: text]", "list[text] | tuple[text]" and "json | map[json, text]" are legal. CITED canon.mjs typeKey, inJson, covers (FINDINGS #65 #74 #79)
tuple, a map never a record, and only json or a union holding json covers json); used by R5
SAME     A and B are the same type up to order: the same kind and, recursively, the same members, where the alts of a union
and the fields of a record (a field = its name, compared exactly, and its tree) compare as SETS, while tuple
items, the list item and the map key and val compare in order
JSON     A is the scalar json and B is JSON-SHAPED (TABLE JSON_SHAPED)
LIST     both are lists and A's item covers B's item
TUPLE    both are tuples with the same number of items and each A item covers the B item at the same position
MAP      both are maps, A's key covers B's key and A's val covers B's val
RECORD   both are records and every field of A has a field of the same name in B whose tree A's field tree covers (B may
have more fields than A)
A-UNION  A is a union and some alt of A covers B
B-UNION  B is a union and A covers every alt of B
none, bool, f64, text, json -> yes
i64, u64, bytes             -> no
list[X]                     -> yes exactly when X is json-shaped
map[K, V]                   -> yes exactly when K is the scalar text itself (not json, not a union) and V is json-shaped
tuple, record               -> yes exactly when every item (every field's tree) is json-shaped
a union                     -> yes exactly when every alt is json-shaped
Uniqueness -> throws: two PARAMs with the same IDENT, or two fields of one record with the same IDENT (compared exactly, so a and A differ).
A rest parameter anywhere but the last PARAM -> throws (two rest parameters included).

Nesting cap -> throws: a composite ALT (tuple list map record) nested inside more than 15 enclosing composite ALTs. A composite at the top of a PARAM's TYPE or the result TYPE has depth 1, one inside its brackets depth 2, and so on; depth 16 is accepted, 17 throws. Unions add no depth, and siblings do not add up: each PARAM and the result start again at 0.
